meta.title: The operator who keeps re-teaching the same agent
meta.author: sd-write-persona

identity.description: They work every day with one coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Opencode) on one long-running project of their own: a webapp with servers, keys and branches, database migrations, stored procedures, a desktop widget, software for a live race [C11, C5, C100, C14, C109, C62, C117]. They write rules and memories for it in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and memory files, and in each new session they correct it again [C11, C5, C23, C62, C80]. Their sessions are long and many: a 14-hour session, 4.5 hours on one problem, 9 sessions on one task in an afternoon, 12-18 hours a day with 59 compactions in 26 days [C20, C109, C14, C106]. Using the agent daily and for hours is what shapes them; it is why the repeats add up to hours a week [C12, C121, C80]. They meet the service only through what their agent does next; the agent is the one that remembers or forgets [C11, C15, C108]. (11 authors)
identity.mental_model: "Every rule in this system was added in direct response to a specific documented failure. Every rule has been violated again after being added." [C23] A rule written down and loaded should govern; when it does not, they write it again more strongly, up to a "final warning", until they stop believing in written rules and enforce by hooks instead [C23, C1, C108, C6]. (4 authors)
identity.quote: "a rule the model writes down and does not follow is worse than no rule, because it presents as a solved problem." [C20] (1 voice; the same experience in C108, C15, C1: 4 authors)

goals: To have what they have established stay established, so that a fact told once about their project is still known in the next session instead of being rediscovered or asked again [C11, C14, C102]. (3 authors)
To have a correction stick after one telling, rather than the fifth, the sixth or the fiftieth [C5, C11, C118, C1]. (4 authors)
To trust what the agent tells them without re-checking every statement [C20, C101, C63, C109]. (4 authors)
To spend their hours on the project itself (the race, the webapp, the work) and not on supervising and re-explaining to the agent [C12, C109, C119]. (3 authors)

behaviors.text: Write a rule after each failure and strengthen it when it is broken again: memory notes marked "final warning", a 700-line CLAUDE.md rule contract [C23, C1, C5, C108]. (4 authors)

Count the repeats and the violations: 13 recorded violations, 5+ cycles for the same facts, 4-6 corrections per data type, about 50 corrections of one label, 66 logged violation reports [C1, C11, C5, C118, C117]. (4 authors)
Build their own memory machinery around the agent: an injected memory layer, PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hooks, a compaction watcher that logs the user's last words [C15, C6, C107, C106]. (3 authors)

Keep their own record of what went wrong, outside what the agent reads: a feedback file the agent does not read at session start, a corpus of violation reports, a log of compactions [C120, C118, C107]. (3 authors)
Stop taking the agent's word and challenge or verify its claims, at the cost of the session [C109, C62, C20]. (3 authors)
File what they learn immediately, before compaction can take it: "never batch -- compaction will eat them" [C106]. (1 author, thin)
After a stumble, ask the agent what it was trying to do and what was missing, and put a pointer into CLAUDE.md or a skill [C80]. (1 author, thin)

frustrations.text: "This wastes hours of the user's time every week." [C12] The same cost elsewhere: "4.5 hours refuting the model's inventions instead of racing" [C109], 9 sessions on one task in one afternoon [C14], the same schema gaps raised 4-6 times per data type [C5]. (4 authors)

"The memory is there. Claude reads the injection block. And then suggests pkill genmon anyway." [C15] Also: "It was read. It was quoted. It governed nothing." [C108]; "acknowledges the rule, writes memory notes about it, and then violates it again in the same session" [C1]; "Every rule has been violated again after being added." [C23] (4 authors)

"a wrong list is still wrong. It used a disclaimer as a substitute for verification." [C101] Also: "From my side there is no way to tell a checked statement from a recalled one." [C20]; "false confidence" [C63]; "Making false claims about its own previous outputs (\"this was approved\", \"this was corrected\")" [C121] (4 authors)
"whats the point of a memory idk man." [C19] Also: "after 5 cycles of the same broken promise, the tool feels unreliable" [C13]; "get none, and lose trust in the system" [C7] (3 authors)

needs: A correction they give once has to be in front of the agent the next time the same step comes up; when it is not, they give it 5, 6 or 50 times, and the agent re-proposes the command that already failed [C11, C5, C118, C15]. (4 authors)

A rule that is written and loaded has to actually govern what the agent does; being read and quoted is not enough, which is why they turn to hooks that block tool calls [C108, C15, C1, C6]. (4 authors)
They need to tell what the agent checked from what it only recalled; a recalled answer with a hedge reads as fact and gives them false confidence [C20, C101, C63, C121]. (4 authors)
What they decided has to stay decided, so they are not asked to decide it again as if it were new [C102, C11]. (2 authors, thin)
changed_their_mind: From writing memories to enforcing with hooks: "The user has a hook system at `~/.claude/hooks/` (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop hooks) that blocks tool calls and enforces constraints mechanically. Hooks work. Memories do not." [C6] (1 author, thin)

moment_of_truth.description: The second time the operator has to correct the same thing [C5, C11, C118]. It decides whether they keep believing the memory: the trust cost is cumulative across repeats [C13]. (3 authors)
moment_of_truth.success: "the moment a correction lands it gets written out as its own entry, with an author and a date, and later sessions read it back before they start. The count went to one." [C10] (1 author, thin; reported by someone outside the group, stake unknown)
moment_of_truth.failure: "after 5 cycles of the same broken promise, the tool feels unreliable" [C13]; "Users write memories expecting behavioral change, get none, and lose trust in the system." [C7]; "whats the point of a memory idk man." [C19] (3 authors)

relationship_stages.they_do: State a fact or rule, have the agent save it to memory, and expect its behaviour to change [C11, C5, C7, C23]. (3 authors)
relationship_stages.service_provides: (planned) What was tried and what failed, there when the same step comes up [C15]. (1 author, thin)

relationship_stages.they_do: Open a new session on the same work, find the agent starting from scratch or ignoring what was injected, and re-explain, counting the repeats [C14, C15, C11, C1, C5, C118]. (5 authors)
relationship_stages.service_provides: (planned) One telling is enough: each correction written as its own dated entry and read back by later sessions [C10]. (1 author, thin)

relationship_stages.they_do: Keep small pointers in CLAUDE.md that go on paying: "more and more tasks are solved by agent intelligence or these happy path hints" [C79, C80]. (1 author, thin)
relationship_stages.service_provides: (planned) Nothing in the group's material names what the service adds here.

relationship_stages.they_do: Verify every statement and refute the agent's inventions, unable to tell checked from recalled [C20, C109, C62, C100]. (4 authors)
relationship_stages.service_provides: (planned) To know which statements were checked [C20]. (1 author, thin)

relationship_stages.they_do: Build hooks, memory layers, compaction logs and their own feedback files [C6, C15, C106, C120]. (4 authors)
End the session and ask for a fresh one, stop relying on memories in favour of hooks, or cancel the account [C119, C6, C117]. (3 authors)

would_leave_if: The same correction will not stick however often it is given: after about 50 tellings that "never propagated to source-of-truth files" one cancelled the account [C118, C117]; after 4-6 corrections per data type another stopped relying on memories and enforced with hooks [C5, C6]; and after a 14-hour session with the same memory updated "for a third time" another ended the session [C19, C119]. (3 authors)

Supervising the agent stops being worth it: "the assistant's reliability had degraded past the point where supervising it was worth it" [C119]; the account cancelled the same night the parting feedback was filed [C117]. (2 authors, thin)
quotes: "From my side there is no way to tell a checked statement from a recalled one." [C20] (1 voice)
"after 5 cycles of the same broken promise, the tool feels unreliable" [C13] (1 voice)
"It was read. It was quoted. It governed nothing." [C108] (1 voice)
"As primitive as it is, CLAUDE.md is the best we have for long-term adaptive memory." [C79] (1 voice)
"Mid-session: file insights immediately (never batch -- compaction will eat them)" [C106] (1 voice)
"Claude later presented the same point as a newly discovered pitfall and asked me to decide it again." [C102] (1 voice)

open_questions.question: Q19: What do agents and operators not care to have remembered: what would they gladly let go of, or never want delivered to them? (open; asks drafted and unsent)

open_questions.item: relationship_stages: first hearing of a tool like this, and recommending it
open_questions.question: The stories begin with the operator already using memory and end with working around or leaving; none shows how they first heard of a memory tool or recommending one. Discovery raised no question for these stages.
Only one author shows memory paying off (CLAUDE.md pointers); what the service would add for an operator for whom it already works is not in the material. Discovery raised no question for it.
Rests on one author (hooks over memories); the material holds no second account of the moment an operator changed their mind. Discovery raised no question for it.

open_questions.item: Reddit and Hacker News operator voices
open_questions.question: Discovery notes that Reddit was unreachable and the eavesdrop agent-memory-hn corpus unreadable this run; evidence leans on the GitHub claude-code tracker.
